lessons.title: Three-Dimensional Geometry

explanation_sections.title: Three-Dimensional Geometry
explanation_sections.body:
Three-dimensional geometry applies Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry to lengths, angles and
positions in solids. The angle between a line and a plane is measured between the line and its
projection onto the plane.

lessons.source_reference: ElimuQuest Mathematics Curriculum Draft v1, PDF pp. 17-18
lessons.author: ElimuQuest

questions.prompt: A cuboid measures 3 cm × 4 cm × 12 cm. Find its space diagonal.
A vertical pole is 8 m high and a ground point is 6 m from its base. Find the distance to the top.
Explain the difference between angles measured from a horizontal and a vertical reference.
questions.correct_answer: They use perpendicular reference directions and are complementary when in the same plane.

questions.prompt: Give an example of a line perpendicular to the base plane of a cuboid.
